BH: B"H / Boruch Hashem / Blessed is He
content:
B"H

# Final Execution Plan

The Awtsmoos creates every layer anew; this execution plan moves only where observed evidence leads it through.
Awtsmoos.com will be changed by complete vessels, not fragments, and every repaired claim will return to runtime proof.

## Stage A — Baseline And Ownership

1. Capture branch, HEAD, remotes, working tree, recent commit, package scripts, server processes, ports, and deployment files.
2. Classify current modified/untracked files, including concurrent-agent work, without discarding anything.
3. Inspect nested agent instructions beneath `geelooy/apps`, shared libraries, server routing, tests, and deployment areas if present.

## Stage B — `/apps` Forensics

4. Enumerate the complete `/apps` tree and read its HTML, module entrypoints, CSS, data, and referenced shared files.
5. Search for `apps-filter.js`, `foundation.js`, favicon references, module/import maps, service workers, and all imports reachable from the entry module.
6. Reproduce `/apps` through the actual running server with Chrome and capture site-owned console errors, failed requests, response headers, redirects, and wrong MIME types.
7. Directly request the failed resources and trace their server/static route ownership.
8. Search recent Git history for path/rename evidence around failed resources.

## Stage C — Whole-Surface Discovery

9. Inventory actual page entrypoints under `geelooy`, with route provenance.
10. Inventory shared JS/API clients and public server APIs used by those pages.
11. Reuse existing route/runtime/static-reference audit tooling when sound; otherwise create small focused modules for missing capabilities.
12. Produce a machine-readable baseline of page families, resource failures, runtime exceptions, API failures, and CSS/static defects.

## Stage D — Actual Rewrite Selection

No production file is pre-approved by filename. After Stages A-C, create a new non-overwriting `09_DISCOVERED_ACTUAL_FILE_PLAN.md` naming every file that will actually be replaced and why. Each selected file must have complete-read evidence, caller/consumer tracing, and tests or runtime witnesses.

## Stage E — Implementation

13. Rewrite complete files only.
14. Resolve systemic static routing/MIME/fallback defects before local page work.
15. Resolve shared API transport/contract defects before duplicative caller patches.
16. Resolve shared UI/CSS foundation defects before page-local CSS, while preserving localized scoping.
17. Repair every discovered page-specific runtime/static defect.
18. Keep human-authored executable source modular and small, using tabs and complete JSDoc for every function parameter and return contract.
19. Add root-cause regression tests and audit tooling alongside implementation.

## Stage F — First Readback And Delta

20. Read every touched file fully.
21. Create `10_FIRST_PASS_DELTA.md` comparing original plans to actual writes and listing every missing obligation.
22. If delta exists, perform a second complete-file write pass only on affected files.
23. Re-read all touched files again.
24. Create `11_SECOND_PASS_DELTA.md`; if anything still remains, perform a final third complete-file pass and re-read.

## Stage G — Verification

25. Run syntax/import checks, relevant unit/integration suites, static asset/reference tests, and API tests.
26. Run the complete practical page/runtime audit, including `/apps` and representative authenticated/unauthenticated paths.
27. Run responsive/UI checks at mobile, tablet, desktop, and cinema-wide viewports plus reduced-motion and keyboard-focused acceptance on representative complex pages.
28. Verify zero site-owned `/apps` console errors, no failed module loads, correct JavaScript MIME, and no unintended 404 favicon/foundation requests.
29. Create `12_FINAL_VERIFICATION_LEDGER.md` with exact commands/results and remaining external blockers, if any.

## Stage H — Git, Push, Deployment

30. Re-run Git status and inspect every changed path and diff.
31. Classify unrelated changes; include safe user/concurrent work as requested, but never publish secrets or local-only hazardous artifacts.
32. Commit the complete safe requested tree and push the canonical GitHub branch.
33. Verify local HEAD equals remote branch HEAD.
34. Follow the repository's real deployment mechanism rather than inventing a parallel path.
35. Verify the canonical deployed URL independently, record live commit/version evidence where exposed, and repeat the runtime audit against production.
36. Create `13_DEPLOYMENT_RECEIPT.md` and close `REMAINING_WORK` only when all evidence agrees.

## NEXT_ACTION

Read back the planning directory, then begin Stage A with Git/process/deployment baseline inspection.
